discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and correlated electrons
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene layers twisted by about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions should dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers built such devices with a controlled 'tear-and-stack' technique. Their transport measurements showed gate-tunable correlated insulating states and, right next to them, superconductivity. That turned a theoretical curiosity into a new materials platform. One clean device can now be gated continuously through insulating, superconducting, magnetic and topological phases, including quantum anomalous Hall and fractional Chern states in moiré systems. This 'twistronics' has changed how condensed-matter physicists work. Stacking angle is now a design parameter, and hundreds of groups worldwide now study strongly correlated and topological matter in van der Waals heterostructures. Few recent ideas combine such a simple prediction, such elegant experiments and such far-reaching consequences.
